l: tax question, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The Pharisees' disciples and the Herodians ask Jesus whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, hoping to entrap him. Jesus calls them hypocrites, has them identify the image on a denarius as Caesar's, and says to give Caesar what is Caesar's and God what is God's, and they marvel and leave.

l: resurrection, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: has_condition no marriage [people are like angels in heaven] The Sadducees deny the resurrection and use a case of seven brothers to challenge it. Jesus says that in the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage but are like God's angels, and that God is the God of the living.

l: seven brothers, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: count seven [brothers who each married the same woman] In the Sadducees' hypothetical, the seven brothers each marry the same woman in turn after the previous brother dies without offspring. The Sadducees use this to ask whose wife she will be in the resurrection.

l: woman (wife of the seven brothers), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: married seven brothers [in succession, each after the previous died] In the Sadducees' puzzle, she is married to the first brother, then to each of the others after each dies without offspring, and she dies last. The Sadducees ask whose wife she will be in the resurrection, and Jesus answers that people neither marry nor are given in marriage there.

l: lawyer (one of the Pharisees), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_a Pharisee A lawyer among the Pharisees asks Jesus, testing him, which is the greatest commandment in the law. Jesus answers with love of God and love of neighbor.

l: greatest commandment, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: content love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind [first and great commandment] Jesus says the first and great commandment is to love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul and mind. The second is to love your neighbor as yourself, and the whole law and the prophets depend on these two.

l: hypocrisy and religious show, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: characterizes scribes and the Pharisees [outwardly righteous, inwardly hypocrisy and iniquity] Jesus describes the scribes and Pharisees as acting to be seen by men: broad phylacteries, enlarged fringes, places of honor, salutations, and titles like 'Rabbi'. He compares them to cleaned cups and whitened tombs that look good outside but are full of extortion, uncleanness, hypocrisy, and iniquity within. He contrasts this with humility, saying whoever exalts himself will be humbled and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

l: false christs and false prophets, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: performs great signs and wonders [to lead astray even the chosen ones if possible] Many will come in Jesus's name claiming to be the Christ and will lead many astray. They will show great signs and wonders to deceive even the chosen ones if possible, and people are told not to believe claims that he is in the wilderness or the inner rooms.

l: end of the age, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The disciples ask for its sign. Jesus says wars, rumors of wars, famines, plagues, and earthquakes are only the beginning of birth pains and that the end is not yet. The end will come after the Good News of the Kingdom is preached in the whole world as a testimony to all nations.

l: coming of the Son of Man, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The coming of the Son of Man, described by Jesus in Chapter 24. It will be visible like lightning from east to west. After the suffering, his sign appears, tribes mourn, and he comes on the clouds with power and glory, sending angels to gather the chosen. Only the Father knows the day and hour; it arrives unexpectedly, as in Noah's days.

l: tribulation, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The tribulation is a period of unparalleled suffering, greater than any since the world's beginning, following the abomination of desolation when those in Judea must flee. Its days are shortened for the chosen ones' sake, and immediately afterward the sun and moon darken and stars fall.

l: servant (faithful and wise), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A faithful and wise servant, described by Jesus in Chapter 24, is set over his lord's household to give food in due season; found doing so on the lord's arrival, he is blessed and set over everything.

l: evil servant, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: An evil servant who believes his lord is delaying, beats fellow servants and eats and drinks with drunkards; his lord arrives unexpectedly, cuts him in pieces, and assigns him a place with hypocrites amid weeping and grinding of teeth.

l: ten virgins, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: takes lamps [went out to meet the bridegroom] The ten virgins took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom, and all slumbered and slept while he delayed. At midnight a cry announced his coming and all arose and trimmed their lamps, but only five were ready to go in.

l: bridegroom, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The bridegroom delayed, then came at midnight after a cry announced him. He took those who were ready into the wedding feast, the door was shut, and he told the late virgins who cried 'Lord, Lord' that he did not know them.

l: servant with five talents, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A servant given five talents according to his ability trades immediately, doubles them to ten, and is praised by his lord as good and faithful, promised many things and the lord's joy.

l: servant with two talents, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A servant given two talents according to his ability trades and gains two more; his lord praises him as good and faithful, setting him over many things and welcoming him into his joy.

l: servant with one talent, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A servant given one talent according to his ability buries it out of fear of his hard lord. Judged wicked and slothful for not earning interest, he loses the talent and is cast into outer darkness as an unprofitable servant.

l: sheep, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_placed right hand [of the King] The sheep are set on the King's right hand and called blessed of his Father. They inherit the Kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world because they fed, gave drink to, took in, clothed, and visited him in the least of these.

l: goats, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The goats are a group placed at the King's left hand, cursed and condemned to eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels because they failed to feed, clothe, or visit him, ending in eternal punishment.

l: righteous, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The righteous are those who inherit the Kingdom prepared from the world's foundation; they ask when they served the King, learn that helping the least of his brothers served him, and enter eternal life.

l: Caiaphas, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_a high priest Caiaphas is the high priest in whose court the chief priests, scribes, and elders plot against Jesus. Jesus is led to him for trial, and he adjures Jesus to say whether he is the Christ, the Son of God. He tears his clothing and declares Jesus's answer blasphemy.

l: Passover, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Jesus says the Passover is two days away and that he will be delivered up to be crucified then. On the first day of unleavened bread the disciples prepare the Passover at a certain person's house in the city, where Jesus eats it with the twelve.

l: Last Supper (Passover meal), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A Passover meal on the first day of unleavened bread, attended by Jesus and the twelve disciples. Jesus foretells betrayal by one who dipped his hand in the dish, telling Judas 'You said it.' He gives bread as his body and the cup as his covenant blood, anticipates drinking anew in his Father's Kingdom, then they sing a hymn and go to the Mount of Olives.

l: Gethsemane, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_a place [where Jesus prayed] Jesus brings the disciples to Gethsemane, taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee further with him, and says his soul is exceedingly sorrowful to death. He prays three times that the cup pass unless it is the Father's will, finding the disciples asleep each time. Judas and the crowd arrive there while he is still speaking.

l: betrayal and arrest of Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: signal kiss from Judas [sign for identifying Jesus] Judas arrives with a great multitude with swords and clubs from the chief priests and elders and gives the sign of a kiss, greeting Jesus as Rabbi. Jesus calls him friend, is seized, and rebukes the follower who cuts off the servant's ear, saying he could ask the Father for more than twelve legions of angels and that this fulfills the Scriptures. All the disciples then leave him and flee.

l: trial before the council, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A night trial of Jesus before the council at Caiaphas the high priest's house. After false testimony and two witnesses' temple claim, Jesus, silent until adjured, answers 'You have said so' and speaks of the Son of Man; the council declares him worthy of death, and some abuse him.

l: Peter's denial, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: occurs_in court of the high priest While Jesus is tried, Peter sits in the court and is identified as a companion of Jesus by a maid, another person, and bystanders. He denies it three times, the last with cursing and swearing, saying 'I don't know the man.' The rooster crows, he remembers Jesus's prediction, and he goes out and weeps bitterly.

l: Pontius Pilate, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Pontius Pilate is a governor with a wife and a custom of releasing one prisoner at the feast. He questions Jesus, heeds his wife's warning and the crowd, washes his hands, releases Barabbas, hands Jesus over to be crucified, then grants his body to Joseph and orders the tomb guarded.

l: Barabbas, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: is_a notable prisoner Barabbas is described as a notable prisoner. The crowd chooses him over Jesus, and Pilate releases him.

l: multitude, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: has_state persuaded by chief priests [to ask for Barabbas] The multitude, persuaded by the chief priests and elders, asks for Barabbas and repeatedly cries 'Let him be crucified!' When Pilate washes his hands, all the people answer, 'May his blood be on us and on our children!'

l: crucifixion of Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Jesus is flogged, mocked, and led out; Simon of Cyrene carries the cross. At Golgotha he is crucified between two robbers, his clothing divided by lot, under a 'King of the Jews' sign. Mocked by all, he dies amid darkness, a torn veil, an earthquake, opened tombs, and the centurion's declaration.

l: Mary Magdalene, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: followed Jesus [from Galilee, serving him] Mary Magdalene comes with the other Mary at dawn to see the tomb. She hears the angel's message, runs with fear and great joy to tell the disciples, meets Jesus, takes hold of his feet, and worships him.

l: Mary the mother of James and Joses, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The other Mary goes with Mary Magdalene to see the tomb at dawn on the first day of the week. She hears the angel announce the resurrection, hurries to tell the disciples, and takes hold of Jesus' feet and worships him when he meets her.

l: Joseph of Arimathaea, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: Joseph of Arimathaea, a rich disciple of Jesus, asks Pilate for Jesus' body, wraps it in clean linen, lays it in his own new rock-cut tomb, and seals it with a large stone.

l: tomb, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: has_state sealed and guarded [secured by chief priests and Pharisees] Joseph's new tomb, cut out in the rock, receives Jesus' body and is closed with a large stone while Mary Magdalene and the other Mary sit opposite. The next day the chief priests and Pharisees, recalling Jesus' saying about rising after three days, have it secured with a guard and a sealed stone at Pilate's permission.

l: women (Mary Magdalene and the other Mary), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A group of women, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary, visit the tomb, are told by an angel that Jesus has risen, leave with fear and joy, meet and worship Jesus, and carry his message to Galilee.

l: angel (angel of the Lord), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: An angel of the Lord descends from the sky amid a great earthquake, rolls away the stone from the tomb, and sits on it, with an appearance like lightning and clothing white as snow. He tells the women not to be afraid, shows them where Jesus lay, announces that Jesus has risen, and instructs them to tell the disciples that Jesus goes before them into Galilee.

l: tomb (Jesus' tomb), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: has_part stone [rolled away by the angel] The tomb is visited by the women at dawn on the first day of the week. Its stone is rolled away by the angel, who sits on it, and the women are shown the place where Jesus had lain, which is empty because he has risen.

l: guards (at Jesus' tomb), The Gospel According to Matthew
s: reports_to chief priests [told what had happened] The guards shake with fear of the angel and become like dead men. Some go into the city and report all that happened to the chief priests, then accept a large amount of silver and spread the story that the disciples stole the body while they slept.

l: resurrection of Jesus, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: The angel declares that Jesus has risen from the dead just as he said, and the empty tomb is shown to the women. Jesus then appears to the women and later to the eleven disciples in Galilee, who worship him though some doubt.

l: story of the stolen body, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: A rumor, paid for by chief priests and elders, claims Jesus' disciples stole his body by night while guards slept; soldiers take the money and comply, and the story spreads among the Jews, persisting until the time of writing.

l: Great Commission, The Gospel According to Matthew
s: In Chapter 28, on a Galilean mountain, Jesus commands the eleven to make disciples of all nations, baptizing in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and teaching obedience to his commands, grounded in his authority and promising constant presence.

l: The Good News According to Mark
s: This document is the Gospel of Mark ("The Good News According to Mark"), sixteen chapters presenting Jesus Christ, the Son of God, from his baptism to his resurrection. Jesus is the central figure; the twelve disciples, especially Peter, James, John and Andrew, are his constant companions, while John the Baptizer, the scribes, Pharisees, chief priests, Herod and Pilate shape the conflict around him. Chapter 1 opens with John baptizing in the Jordan. Jesus is baptized, declared the beloved Son, tempted in the wilderness, then preaches God's Kingdom in Galilee, calls his first followers, casts out an unclean spirit and heals many. Chapters 2 and 3 show healings, the forgiving of a paralytic's sins, the call of Levi, and disputes over fasting and the Sabbath. Opposition hardens as the Pharisees and Herodians plot to destroy him, he appoints the twelve, and scribes accuse him of having Beelzebul. Chapters 4 to 6 bring parables of the sower and the Kingdom, the calming of the storm, the Gadarene demoniac, Jairus's daughter and the woman with the flow of blood. Rejected in his own country, he sends the twelve out. The account of John's beheading by Herod follows, then the feeding of five thousand and Jesus walking on the sea. Chapters 7 and 8 treat the tradition of the elders and what truly defiles, the Syrophoenician woman's daughter, healing the deaf and the blind, and a feeding of four thousand. At Caesarea Philippi Peter declares Jesus the Christ, and Jesus foretells his suffering, death and resurrection, calling followers to take up their cross. Chapters 9 and 10 mark the turn toward Jerusalem: the transfiguration, the boy with a mute spirit, further predictions of his death, teaching on greatness, children, divorce and riches, the request of James and John, and the healing of Bartimaeus. Chapters 11 to 13 cover the entry into Jerusalem, the cursed fig tree, the cleansing of the temple, challenges to his authority, the vineyard parable, questions about taxes, resurrection and the greatest commandment, the widow's coins, and his prophecy of the temple's fall and the coming of the Son of Man, with a call to watch. Chapters 14 and 15 narrate the Passion: the plot, anointing, Judas's betrayal, the last supper, Gethsemane, arrest, condemnation, Peter's three denials, trial before Pilate, Barabbas's release, crucifixion, death, and burial by Joseph of Arimathaea. Chapter 16 closes with the women finding the empty tomb and hearing that Jesus has risen, his appearances, the commission to preach to all creation, and his ascension, after which the disciples preach everywhere.

l: Jesus, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus is the central figure of the Gospel of Mark: a Nazarene of Galilee, a carpenter and son of Mary with brothers James, Joses, Judah and Simon and sisters, who is declared beloved Son of God by a voice from the sky, by unclean spirits, and later by a centurion. He is also confessed as the Christ by Peter, and he affirms it himself before the high priest. He calls himself Son of Man and is addressed as Teacher and Lord. The account opens with his coming from Nazareth, baptism by John, and forty days of temptation. He then preaches God's Kingdom in Galilee, with a home in Capernaum. He calls disciples and appoints the twelve, teaching with authority unlike the scribes. He casts out unclean spirits, heals the sick, and forgives sins. He heals the withered hand and claims lordship over the Sabbath. He likens himself to a physician for sinners and to a bridegroom. He teaches in parables, calms a storm, raises Jairus's daughter, feeds multitudes out of compassion, and walks on the sea. He is rejected in his home country, and his teaching, such as that food does not defile, puts him in conflict with Pharisees and scribes. After Peter's confession he repeatedly foretells his suffering, death and rising, and teaches that the Son of Man came to serve and give his life as a ransom. He rides a young donkey into Jerusalem, curses the fig tree, cleanses the temple, and teaches on faith, prayer and forgiveness. He refuses to disclose the source of his authority to his questioners. He says that only the Father knows the day and hour. He is betrayed, arrested, condemned, and handed to Pilate, who asks if he is King of the Jews. He is mocked, crucified between two robbers, and cries out before dying. Women who followed and served him from Galilee are present. He is laid in a tomb, then announced as risen. He appears to Mary Magdalene and to the eleven, commissions them to preach to all creation, goes before the disciples to Galilee as he said, is received up into heaven, and sits at God's right hand.

l: John, The Good News According to Mark
s: The records bring together two figures named John, which the text itself distinguishes. The first is a wilderness baptizer who wears camel's hair and a leather belt, eats locusts and wild honey, and preaches repentance in the Jordan. He is a messenger sent to prepare the Lord's way, announces a mightier one who will baptize in the Holy Spirit, baptizes Jesus, is taken into custody, and is regarded by all the people as a prophet. The second is John, son of Zebedee and brother of James, nicknamed Boanerges. Jesus calls him from mending nets, and he asks with James for seats of glory.

l: Peter, The Good News According to Mark
s: Peter, also called Simon, is a Galilean fisherman and brother of Andrew, whose mother-in-law lived in his house. Jesus calls him from his nets, and he immediately follows, becoming a disciple, one of the twelve, and receiving the name Peter from Jesus. He addresses Jesus as Rabbi and declares him the Christ, yet rebukes Jesus over predicted suffering and is rebuked in turn as thinking the things of men. On the mountain with James and John, he fearfully proposes three tents. In Gethsemane he vows never to deny Jesus, even in death, but falls asleep, then follows the arrested Jesus into the high priest's courtyard, denies him three times, and weeps on remembering Jesus' words.

l: James, The Good News According to Mark
s: James, son of Zebedee and brother of John, appears in Chapter 10 asking Jesus for seats at his right and left in glory; Jesus says they will share his cup and baptism, but seats are prepared.

l: Satan, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_a ruler of demons [as alleged by scribes] Jesus argues that Satan cannot cast out Satan, since a kingdom or house divided against itself cannot stand and Satan, if divided, would come to an end. He also likens Satan to a strong man whose house can be plundered only after he is bound.

l: God, The Good News According to Mark
s: God is presented in Mark as the God of the living, not the dead, and of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Early on he is the Father of Jesus Christ, whom a heavenly voice calls his beloved Son; Jesus preaches God's Kingdom as at hand. Later the Kingdom is said to come with power, and the voice from the cloud tells the three to listen to Jesus. Jesus teaches that God made male and female and joins husband and wife, that only God is good, and that with God all things are possible, including salvation. Finally, God is the one Lord, to be loved wholly, which matters more than sacrifices.

l: Holy Spirit, The Good News According to Mark
s: The Holy Spirit speaks through disciples when they are delivered up; blaspheming against it is never forgiven, bringing eternal condemnation, as Jesus warns after being accused of an unclean spirit.

l: Jerusalem, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus approaches and enters Jerusalem, where crowds welcome him, and he repeatedly goes into the temple there, returning to Bethany in the evenings. The chief priests, scribes, and elders in the city plan to destroy him and question his authority.

l: baptism of repentance, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_for forgiveness of sins John preaches and carries out the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins in the Jordan river. People from all Judea and Jerusalem go out to him, are baptized, and confess their sins. John contrasts it with the coming baptism in the Holy Spirit.

l: Good News, The Good News According to Mark
s: The Good News is the message about Jesus Christ, the Son of God. Jesus first preaches God's Kingdom in Galilee, urging repentance and belief. He later commands the eleven to preach it to the whole creation, promising salvation to believers, and the disciples preach it everywhere.

l: God's Kingdom, The Good News According to Mark
s: God's Kingdom is a theme proclaimed by Jesus as at hand. In Chapter 4, its mystery is given to the disciples, not outsiders, and it is likened to seed growing by itself until harvest and to a tiny mustard seed becoming a great plant. In Chapter 10, it belongs to little children, must be received like one, and is hard for the rich to enter.

l: John the Baptizer, The Good News According to Mark
s: John the Baptizer, a righteous and holy man with disciples, rebuked Herod for taking his brother's wife, was imprisoned, then beheaded at Herodias's request; his disciples buried his corpse in a tomb.

l: scribes, The Good News According to Mark
s: believes only God can forgive sins [regarded Jesus' claim as blasphemy] Some scribes sitting there reason in their hearts that Jesus blasphemes by forgiving sins, since only God can do so. Jesus perceives this and challenges them. Later, scribes of the Pharisees' party ask his disciples why he eats with tax collectors and sinners.

l: man with an unclean spirit, The Good News According to Mark
s: A man in the Capernaum synagogue, possessed by an unclean spirit, cries out and calls Jesus the Holy One of God; Jesus rebukes the spirit, which convulses him and leaves, amazing onlookers.

l: leper, The Good News According to Mark
s: A man with leprosy kneels before Jesus begging to be made clean; moved with compassion, Jesus touches and heals him instantly. Told to stay silent, he spreads the news widely, so Jesus can no longer enter cities openly.

l: paralytic, The Good News According to Mark
s: A paralyzed man on a mat, lowered through a roof to Jesus, who declares his sins forgiven, then commands him to rise; he takes his mat and walks home publicly.

l: four people (who carried the paralytic), The Good News According to Mark
s: Four people carry the paralytic to Jesus. Unable to get near him because of the crowd, they remove and break up the roof and lower the mat, and Jesus sees their faith.

l: Pharisees, The Good News According to Mark
s: The Pharisees are a religious group, often joined by scribes, who persistently oppose Jesus. They hold to the tradition of the elders, practice fasting with their disciples, and wash hands and forearms before eating. Jesus calls them hypocrites who set aside God's commandment to keep their tradition, and warns his disciples against their yeast. The account unfolds as a escalating series of confrontations. First they question his eating with tax collectors and sinners, his disciples' lack of fasting, and Sabbath grain-plucking. Then they watch him heal on the Sabbath and conspire with the Herodians to destroy him. Later, scribes from Jerusalem fault his disciples' unwashed hands. They seek a sign from heaven, test him on divorce, and finally, with the Herodians, try to trap him with words about paying taxes to Caesar. Jesus answers them each time, and they marvel at the last.

l: Levi, The Good News According to Mark
s: Levi, son of Alphaeus, is a tax collector who, called by Jesus while sitting at his tax office, rises to follow him and then hosts tax collectors and sinners at a meal.

l: tax collectors and sinners, The Good News According to Mark
s: follows Jesus [many of them] Many tax collectors and sinners sit down with Jesus and his disciples at the table in the house, and they follow him. Jesus says he came to call sinners to repentance, not the righteous.

l: disciples (Jesus's disciples), The Good News According to Mark
s: The disciples are the twelve followers who accompany Jesus throughout the records, appearing as a group whose closeness to him is repeatedly matched by their lack of understanding. Early on they eat with tax collectors and sinners, do not fast while the bridegroom is with them, and pluck grain on the Sabbath, with Jesus defending them. They are then sent out in pairs with authority over unclean spirits, distribute loaves and fish, and gather twelve baskets, then seven baskets, of leftovers. Yet they are terrified when they see Jesus walking on the sea, and their hearts are described as hardened because they had not understood about the loaves. Jesus repeatedly asks whether they yet understand, including over the warning about yeast. They are taught about his coming suffering and told to tell no one about him. They fail to cast the spirit out of the boy, which Jesus says comes out only by prayer and fasting. They do not grasp his predictions of his death, are afraid to ask, argue about who is greatest, forbid an outsider casting out demons, rebuke those bringing children, and the ten become indignant at James and John. Peter says they have left all to follow him. Two fetch the donkey as instructed, and they hear the fig tree cursed. Peter, James, John, and Andrew privately ask about the temple's fate and are warned of deception, persecution, and the need to endure, watch, and pray. At the Passover the twelve each ask 'Surely not I?' when betrayal is foretold by Jesus. All vow not to deny him, but they all leave him and flee when he is arrested.

l: fasting, The Good News According to Mark
s: will_resume_for disciples (Jesus' disciples) [when the bridegroom is taken away] John's disciples and the Pharisees fast, while Jesus' disciples do not. Jesus says they cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them, but will fast in the days when he is taken away. He adds the sayings about unshrunk cloth on an old garment and new wine in old wineskins.

l: forgiveness of sins, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_attributed_to God [according to the scribes] Jesus tells the paralytic his sins are forgiven, and the scribes consider this blasphemy because only God can forgive sins. Jesus says he heals the man so they may know the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.

l: Sabbath, The Good News According to Mark
s: The Sabbath is a day of rest at the center of conflict between Jesus and the Pharisees. In Chapter 2 Jesus defends his disciples' plucking grain, saying it was made for man and he is its lord. In Chapter 3 he asks whether it is lawful to do good or save life; opponents stay silent.

l: David, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus says David, speaking in the Holy Spirit, said 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet.' Because David calls the Christ Lord, Jesus asks how he can be David's son.

l: sea, The Good News According to Mark
s: The sea is the setting where Jesus teaches the multitude from a boat while they stand on the shore. During the evening crossing, Jesus commands it, "Peace! Be still!", and it becomes calm, so that the disciples marvel that it obeys him.

l: man with withered hand (synagogue), The Good News According to Mark
s: A man with a withered hand in a synagogue is told by Jesus to stand and stretch out his hand, which is restored healthy like the other.

l: Herodians, The Good News According to Mark
s: Some Herodians are sent with Pharisees to trap Jesus with words about paying taxes to Caesar. They marvel greatly at his answer.

l: multitude (following Jesus), The Good News According to Mark
s: A great multitude drawn from Galilee, Judea, Jerusalem, Idumaea, beyond the Jordan, and around Tyre and Sidon follows Jesus after hearing of his deeds. The diseased press to touch him, so he requests a boat; crowds grow so tight they cannot eat, and a multitude sits around him when his family arrives.

l: the twelve apostles, The Good News According to Mark
s: The twelve apostles are a group Jesus appoints on the mountain to be with him, be sent out to preach, and hold authority to heal sicknesses and cast out demons. Named members include Simon Peter, James, John, and Andrew; the list ends with Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.

l: Judas Iscariot, The Good News According to Mark
s: Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, betrays Jesus: he goes to the chief priests, who promise him money, then at Gethsemane identifies Jesus for arrest with a kiss and "Rabbi! Rabbi!"

l: scribes from Jerusalem, The Good News According to Mark
s: A group of scribes from Jerusalem accuses Jesus of having Beelzebul and casting out demons by the prince of demons; Jesus summons them and answers in parables about divided kingdoms.

l: blasphemy, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_forgivable all except against the Holy Spirit Jesus says all sins and blasphemies of the descendants of man will be forgiven. The exception is blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, which never has forgiveness and brings eternal condemnation.

l: Jesus's mother, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_mother_of Jesus Jesus's mother comes with his brothers and, standing outside, sends word calling him. Jesus responds by asking who his mother and brothers are and says that whoever does God's will is his mother, brother, and sister.

l: Jesus's brothers and sisters, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_sibling_of Jesus Jesus's brothers come with his mother and stand outside calling for him, and the crowd tells him his brothers and sisters are outside looking for him. Jesus answers by naming those sitting around him as his mother and brothers, and says whoever does the will of God is his brother and sister.

l: farmer (parable of the sower), The Good News According to Mark
s: The farmer goes out to sow seed that falls on the road, rocky ground, thorns, and good ground. Jesus explains that the farmer sows the word.

l: seed (the sower's seed), The Good News According to Mark
s: The seed is eaten by birds on the road, scorched on rocky ground for lack of root, and choked among thorns. On good ground it yields thirty, sixty, or one hundred times as much. Jesus identifies the seed with the word sown in people, and in other parables the Kingdom is likened to seed that grows by itself and to a tiny mustard seed that becomes greater than all herbs.

l: multitude (gathered to Jesus), The Good News According to Mark
s: A great multitude gathers to Jesus by the sea, standing on the land while he teaches from the boat. He speaks the word to them in many parables, as they are able to hear it, and then leaves them behind when he and his disciples cross the sea.

l: disciples (those around him with the twelve), The Good News According to Mark
s: Those around Jesus with the twelve ask him privately about the parables and are told that the mystery of God's Kingdom is given to them. Jesus asks whether they understand the parable of the sower and explains everything to them. In the storm they wake him, asking if he cares that they are dying, and after he calms it they are greatly afraid and ask who he is that the wind and sea obey him.

l: parables, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_used_for those who are outside [all things are done in parables to them] Jesus teaches the multitude many things in parables, and speaks to them only in parables, as they are able to hear. He tells the disciples that to those outside all things are done in parables, so that seeing they do not perceive, and he explains everything privately to his own disciples. He says that understanding the sower parable is needed to understand all the parables.

l: the word (of God), The Good News According to Mark
s: The word is what the farmer sows. Satan takes it from those by the road, those on rocky ground receive it with joy but stumble under oppression or persecution, and the cares of the age, riches, and lusts choke it among thorns. Those on good ground hear it, accept it, and bear fruit thirty, sixty, or one hundred times.

l: boat (Jesus's boat), The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus enters a boat and sits in it to teach the multitude on the shore. That evening the disciples take him across the sea in it, with other small boats accompanying. A storm fills the boat with waves while he sleeps on the cushion in the stern.

l: wind storm, The Good News According to Mark
s: fills boat [waves beat into it] A big wind storm arises while Jesus and his disciples cross the sea, and waves beat into the boat until it is nearly filled. Jesus rebukes the wind, it ceases, and a great calm follows.

l: man with an unclean spirit (Gadarenes tombs), The Good News According to Mark
s: A man living in the tombs, possessed by an unclean spirit, is so strong that chains and fetters cannot hold him, and he cries out and cuts himself with stones night and day. He runs to Jesus, is freed of the spirit, and is found clothed and in his right mind. Told to go home, he proclaims what the Lord did in Decapolis, and all marvel.

l: Legion, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_a unclean spirits [demons possessing the man] Legion is the name the unclean spirit gives when Jesus asks, explaining that 'we are many.' The demons beg not to be sent out of the country and ask to be sent into the pigs, and Jesus permits it.

l: pigs (herd near Gadarenes), The Good News According to Mark
s: A herd of about two thousand pigs feeds on a mountainside, is entered by unclean spirits with Jesus' permission, then rushes down the bank into the sea and drowns.

l: Jairus, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jairus is a synagogue ruler and father who begs Jesus to heal his dying little daughter; told she has died, he is urged to believe, and he and his wife then see her raised.

l: Jairus's daughter, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jairus's twelve-year-old daughter, near death and then reported dead, is called asleep by Jesus, who takes her hand and says 'Talitha cumi'; she rises, walks, and is given food.

l: woman with discharge of blood, The Good News According to Mark
s: A woman suffering a discharge of blood for twelve years, worsened despite spending everything on many physicians, touches Jesus' clothes from behind in a crowd, is healed at once, confesses fearfully, and is called 'Daughter' and sent in peace.

l: healing of the bleeding woman, The Good News According to Mark
s: has_cause her faith [stated by Jesus] On the way to Jairus's house, the woman touches Jesus' clothes, her bleeding dries up immediately, and she feels in her body that she is healed. Jesus perceives that power has gone out from him and asks who touched him, then tells her that her faith has made her well.

l: raising of Jairus's daughter, The Good News According to Mark
s: After news a girl has died, Jesus goes to her house with Peter, James, John and her parents, expels the ridiculing mourners, takes her hand, and she rises and walks. Onlookers are amazed; he orders silence and food for her.

l: Herod, The Good News According to Mark
s: Herod is a king married to Herodias, his brother Philip's former wife. He imprisoned John the Baptizer for her sake yet feared him as righteous and holy. At his birthday supper he swore an oath, then reluctantly beheaded John, and later thought Jesus was John risen.

l: Herodias, The Good News According to Mark
s: Herodias, former wife of Herod's brother Philip, opposes John the Baptizer and wants him dead but is blocked by Herod's protection; she then instructs her daughter to request John's head and receives it.

l: daughter of Herodias, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_daughter_of Herodias She came in and danced, pleasing Herod and his guests, and the king offered her whatever she wanted. After consulting her mother, she asked for John's head on a platter, received it, and gave it to her mother.

l: Elijah, The Good News According to Mark
s: has_state has come [was mistreated by people] Elijah appears with Moses and talks with Jesus on the mountain. Jesus tells the disciples that Elijah indeed comes first and restores all things, and that Elijah has already come and people did to him whatever they wanted, as it is written.

l: Herod's birthday banquet, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_hosted_by Herod [on his birthday] Herod made a supper on his birthday for his nobles, high officers, and the chief men of Galilee. During it the daughter of Herodias danced, Herod swore to give her whatever she asked up to half his kingdom, and this led to John's beheading.

l: mission of the twelve, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus sends the twelve out two by two with authority over unclean spirits, allowing only a staff, sandals and one tunic, no bread or money. They stay in one house per place, preach repentance, cast out demons, heal the sick, then report back.

l: multitude, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_like sheep without a shepherd [Jesus had compassion] Many people recognized Jesus and his disciples leaving by boat and ran on foot from all the cities, arriving ahead of them. Jesus had compassion on them as sheep without a shepherd and taught them. They were seated in groups of hundreds and fifties, all ate and were filled, and Jesus then sent them away.

l: feeding of the five thousand, The Good News According to Mark
s: Late in the day in a deserted place, Jesus has disciples feed a crowd; he blesses and breaks five loaves and two fish, all eat and are filled, twelve baskets of pieces remain, and five thousand men ate.

l: loaves and fish, The Good News According to Mark
s: has_quantity five loaves and two fish The disciples found five loaves and two fish among the crowd. Jesus blessed and broke the loaves and divided the fish, and the disciples distributed them. Twelve baskets full of broken pieces and fish remained.

l: Jesus walking on the sea, The Good News According to Mark
s: occurs_at fourth watch of the night [wind contrary to disciples] Jesus sent his disciples ahead by boat to Bethsaida and went up the mountain to pray. About the fourth watch he came to them walking on the sea as they struggled against a contrary wind, and he would have passed by them. They thought him a ghost and cried out, but he told them to cheer up and not be afraid, got into the boat, and the wind ceased.

l: Gennesaret, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_a land across the sea [where the boat moored] After crossing the sea, the boat came to land and moored at Gennesaret. The people recognized Jesus at once and ran around the region bringing the sick on mats to where he was.

l: healing of the sick, The Good News According to Mark
s: has_method touching the fringe of his garment [all who touched were made well] In his own country Jesus laid hands on a few sick people and healed them, and the twelve anointed many sick with oil and healed them. At Gennesaret and in villages, cities, and the country, people laid the sick in marketplaces and begged to touch the fringe of his garment. As many as touched him were made well.

l: scribes, The Good News According to Mark
s: come_from Jerusalem [some of them] Some scribes who came from Jerusalem gather with the Pharisees and join in questioning Jesus about his disciples' unwashed hands. They are included in Jesus' rebuke as hypocrites who hold to the tradition of men.

l: tradition of the elders, The Good News According to Mark
s: includes washings of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and couches The tradition of the elders is described as the practice of the Pharisees and all the Jews of washing hands and forearms before eating, bathing after the marketplace, and washing cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and couches. Jesus calls it a tradition of men that is held tightly while God's commandment is set aside.

l: ritual washing and defilement, The Good News According to Mark
s: The Pharisees treat eating with unwashed hands as defiling. Jesus teaches that nothing entering a man from outside can defile him, since it goes into the stomach and then the latrine, making all foods clean, and that only what proceeds out of the man defiles him.

l: commandment of God, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus says the Pharisees and scribes set aside God's commandment, citing Moses' words to honor father and mother and that whoever speaks evil of them should be put to death. He says their tradition makes void the word of God.

l: Corban, The Good News According to Mark
s: means given to God Corban is a vow, explained as 'given to God,' by which a man says that whatever profit his father or mother might have received from him is Corban. Jesus says this tradition stops a person from doing anything for his parents and so voids God's word.

l: evil things from within the heart, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus lists evil things proceeding from within the heart, including evil thoughts, adulteries, murders, thefts, deceit, blasphemy, pride and foolishness, and declares that all of them come from within and defile the man.

l: Syrophoenician woman, The Good News According to Mark
s: A Greek Syrophoenician woman begs Jesus near Tyre to cast a demon from her little daughter. After he likens her request to throwing children's bread to dogs, her reply about the dogs eating crumbs earns his approval, and she returns home to find her daughter healed.

l: daughter (Syrophoenician woman's daughter), The Good News According to Mark
s: is_freed_of unclean spirit (the demon) [after Jesus' word] The Syrophoenician woman's little daughter has an unclean spirit. After Jesus speaks, her mother finds her laid on the bed with the demon gone out.

l: unclean spirit (the demon), The Good News According to Mark
s: An unclean spirit afflicts the Syrophoenician woman's little daughter. Jesus declares that the demon has gone out of her, and it is found to be gone when the woman reaches home.

l: deaf man with speech impediment, The Good News According to Mark
s: has_condition deaf with speech impediment [before healing] People bring to Jesus a man who is deaf and has an impediment in his speech, begging Jesus to lay his hand on him. Jesus takes him aside privately, and the man's ears are opened and his tongue released so that he speaks clearly.

l: healing of the deaf man, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus heals a deaf man privately, touching his ears and tongue, sighing and saying 'Ephphatha'; the man is instantly healed. Jesus commands silence, yet the news spreads widely, and astonished people say he does all things well.

l: multitude (four thousand), The Good News According to Mark
s: size about four thousand A great multitude has stayed with Jesus three days with nothing to eat. About four thousand eat and are filled, and Jesus sends them away. Later Jesus calls a multitude to himself with his disciples and teaches them about denying oneself and taking up the cross.

l: seven loaves, The Good News According to Mark
s: The disciples report they have seven loaves. Jesus takes them, gives thanks, breaks them, and has the disciples serve the multitude, along with a few small fish he blessed. Seven baskets of broken pieces are left over, and Jesus later recalls this when questioning the disciples.

l: yeast of the Pharisees and Herod, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus warns his disciples to take heed and beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod. The disciples wrongly think he speaks of having no bread, and Jesus rebukes their lack of perception and understanding.

l: blind man, The Good News According to Mark
s: A blind man brought by others to Jesus at Bethsaida; Jesus leads him out of the village, touches his eyes twice, first giving blurry sight, then full clear vision, and sends him home, forbidding him to enter the village.

l: Christ, The Good News According to Mark
s: Christ is a messianic title and figure. In Chapter 8, Peter identifies Jesus as the Christ, and Jesus commands silence about it. In Chapter 12, Jesus questions how the Christ can be David's son when David, in the Holy Spirit, calls him Lord.

l: Jesus's death and resurrection (predicted), The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus repeatedly predicts his own suffering, death, and resurrection. He says the Son of Man must be rejected by elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and rise on the third day. The teaching begins openly in Chapter 8, where Peter's rebuke is itself rebuked. In Chapter 9 he says the Son of Man will be handed to men, and the disciples do not understand. In Chapter 10, nearing Jerusalem, he adds condemnation, delivery to the Gentiles, mocking, spitting, and scourging before rising.

l: chief priests, The Good News According to Mark
s: The chief priests are a group hostile to Jesus, driven by fear of him and of the crowd's astonishment at his teaching. In the temple they seek to destroy him and, with scribes and elders, question his authority while dodging his question for fear of the people. They plot to seize and kill him by deception, welcome Judas's offer of betrayal, and send a multitude to arrest him. They bind and deliver him to Pilate, stir the crowd to demand Barabbas, and mock Jesus at the cross.

l: discipleship and taking up the cross, The Good News According to Mark
s: requires denying oneself [for whoever wants to follow Jesus] Jesus tells the multitude and his disciples that whoever wants to come after him must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow him. He says whoever tries to save his life will lose it, while whoever loses it for his sake and the Good News will save it, and he warns that those ashamed of him and his words will be met with the Son of Man's shame when he comes in glory.

l: scribes, The Good News According to Mark
s: The scribes are a group of religious authorities who fear Jesus and, with chief priests and elders, seek to destroy him and challenge his authority, failing to answer his question about John. Jesus then questions their claim about David's son and warns against their love of honor, exploitation of widows, and pretentious prayers, declaring greater condemnation.

l: father (father of the boy), The Good News According to Mark
s: The father brings his son to Jesus and describes the spirit's long attacks, which have thrown the boy into fire and water since childhood. When Jesus says all things are possible to him who believes, he cries out with tears, "I believe. Help my unbelief!"

l: boy (the possessed son), The Good News According to Mark
s: The boy is seized by a mute spirit that throws him down, makes him foam, grind his teeth, and become rigid. After Jesus commands the spirit out, the boy lies like one dead, and Jesus takes his hand and raises him up, and he arises.

l: mute spirit (the boy's spirit), The Good News According to Mark
s: The mute spirit has afflicted the boy since childhood and convulses him when he is brought to Jesus. Jesus rebukes it as a mute and deaf spirit and commands it to come out and never enter him again, and it leaves after crying out and convulsing him greatly.

l: Transfiguration, The Good News According to Mark
s: On a high mountain, six days after a teaching, Jesus is transformed before Peter, James, and John, his clothing turning dazzling white. Elijah and Moses talk with him, a cloud voice names him beloved Son, and he orders silence until his resurrection.

l: dispute over who was greatest, The Good News According to Mark
s: involves disciples (Jesus's disciples) [on the way to Capernaum] On the way to Capernaum the disciples dispute among themselves about who is the greatest, and they are silent when Jesus asks about it in the house. Jesus sits down, calls the twelve, and says whoever wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all, then sets a little child among them as an example.

l: divorce, The Good News According to Mark
s: has_status allowed by Moses [due to hardness of heart] Jesus says Moses allowed a certificate of divorce because of hardness of heart, but that from creation the two become one flesh, and what God has joined let no man separate. He adds that whoever divorces and marries another commits adultery, whether man or woman.

l: little children (brought to Jesus), The Good News According to Mark
s: Little children are brought to Jesus so that he may touch them, and the disciples rebuke those bringing them. Jesus is indignant, says God's Kingdom belongs to such as these, then takes them in his arms and blesses them.

l: rich man (the man who asked about eternal life), The Good News According to Mark
s: A wealthy man claiming lifelong commandment-keeping runs to Jesus, kneels, and asks how to inherit eternal life. Jesus, loving him, says to sell everything, give to the poor, and follow; he leaves sorrowful, holding great possessions.

l: riches, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus says it is difficult for those who have riches, and hard for those who trust in them, to enter God's Kingdom, comparing it to a camel going through a needle's eye. The disciples are astonished, and Jesus answers that with God all things are possible.

l: Bartimaeus, The Good News According to Mark
s: Bartimaeus, blind beggar and son of Timaeus, sits by the road at Jericho, cries out to Jesus despite rebukes, is called and told his faith healed him, regains sight, and follows Jesus.

l: young donkey (Jesus's mount), The Good News According to Mark
s: A young, never-ridden donkey tied in the street is untied by two disciples because the Lord needs it, then covered with garments and ridden by Jesus toward Jerusalem.

l: temple, The Good News According to Mark
s: The temple in Jerusalem, designated a house of prayer for all nations, is where Jesus enters, returns the next day to drive out sellers and buyers, calls it a den of robbers, and is later challenged by leaders.

l: crowd (people who welcomed Jesus), The Good News According to Mark
s: proclaims kingdom of David [as blessed, coming in the name of the Lord] Many in the crowd spread their garments and cut branches to spread on the road, and those in front and behind cry out "Hosanna" and bless the coming kingdom of David. The whole multitude is also described as astonished at Jesus' teaching, and the people are feared by the leaders.

l: fig tree, The Good News According to Mark
s: A fig tree bearing only leaves, out of season, is cursed by hungry Jesus so no one will eat its fruit again; next morning the disciples find it withered from the roots, Peter noting it.

l: money changers and sellers in the temple, The Good News According to Mark
s: sell_in temple (in Jerusalem) [doves, trading and money changing] Jesus throws out those selling and buying in the temple and overturns the money changers' tables and the seats of the dove sellers. He accuses them of making the house of prayer a den of robbers.

l: triumphal entry, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus rides a borrowed young donkey toward Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives area, with garments and branches spread on the road. Crowds in front and behind cry "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord," and bless the coming kingdom of David.

l: cleansing of the temple, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus enters the temple, throws out sellers and buyers, overturns the money changers' tables and dove sellers' seats, and bars carrying containers through it. He cites that it should be a house of prayer for all nations, and the chief priests and scribes respond by seeking to destroy him.

l: faith and prayer, The Good News According to Mark
s: requires forgiveness [when standing praying] Prompted by the withered fig tree, Jesus tells the disciples to have faith in God, saying whoever without doubt tells a mountain to be cast into the sea will have it. He says whatever is prayed for in belief will be received, and that praying people must forgive others so the Father will forgive them.

l: authority of Jesus, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_questioned_by chief priests [along with scribes and elders] The chief priests, scribes, and elders ask by what authority Jesus does these things and who gave it to him. Jesus answers with a question about John's baptism, and when they say they don't know, he declines to tell them his authority.

l: man who planted a vineyard (parable), The Good News According to Mark
s: owns vineyard (parable) [planted it and rented it out] The man planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a pit for the wine press, built a tower, rented it to farmers, and went to another country. He sent servants and finally his beloved son; Jesus says he will come, destroy the farmers, and give the vineyard to others.

l: vineyard (parable), The Good News According to Mark
s: A parable vineyard, planted with a hedge, wine press pit and tower, is rented out by its owner to farmers, who cast out the son; Jesus says it will pass to others.

l: farmers (parable), The Good News According to Mark
s: mistreat servants (parable) [beat, stoned, killed] The farmers beat one servant, stoned and wounded another, and killed another along with many others. They then killed the heir, casting him out of the vineyard, and Jesus says the lord will destroy them.

l: man traveling (parable), The Good News According to Mark
s: leaves servants and doorkeeper (parable) [given authority and work; doorkeeper to keep watch] In the parable, a man goes to another country, leaving his house, giving authority and work to each servant, and commanding the doorkeeper to keep watch. The lord of the house's return time is unknown, whether evening, midnight, rooster crow, or morning, and he must not find them sleeping when he comes suddenly.

l: beloved son (parable), The Good News According to Mark
s: The vineyard planter's beloved son in a parable, sent last in hope of respect, but recognized as heir by the farmers, killed, and cast out.

l: Parable of the vineyard, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus tells this parable about a man, his vineyard, rebellious farmers, and his murdered son, ending with the lord destroying the farmers and giving the vineyard to others. The leaders perceive it was spoken against them and try to seize him but fear the multitude.

l: Caesar, The Good News According to Mark
s: has_image_on denarius [image and inscription] Caesar's image and inscription are on the denarius that Jesus asks to see. Jesus says to give to Caesar the things that are Caesar's.

l: taxes to Caesar, The Good News According to Mark
s: The Pharisees and Herodians ask whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar. Jesus has a denarius brought, notes it bears Caesar's image, and says to give Caesar what is Caesar's and God what is God's.

l: Sadducees, The Good News According to Mark
s: believe no resurrection [doctrinal position] The Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, ask Jesus about a woman who married seven brothers in turn. Jesus tells them they are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God, and are badly mistaken.

l: resurrection, The Good News According to Mark
s: has_condition no marrying [those raised are like angels in heaven] The Sadducees deny the resurrection and challenge Jesus about it. Jesus says that when people rise they neither marry nor are given in marriage but are like angels in heaven, and that God is God of the living, not the dead.

l: seven brothers and the woman, The Good News According to Mark
s: In the Sadducees' scenario, seven brothers each take the same woman as wife and die without children, and the woman dies last. The Sadducees ask whose wife she will be in the resurrection.

l: scribe (who asked about the greatest commandment), The Good News According to Mark
s: is_not_far_from God’s Kingdom [because he answered wisely] This scribe heard the questioning, saw that Jesus answered well, and asked which commandment is greatest. He affirms Jesus' answer, saying love is more than offerings and sacrifices, and Jesus tells him he is not far from God's Kingdom.

l: greatest commandments, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus' two greatest commandments: first, love the Lord God with all heart, soul, mind, and strength; second, love your neighbor as yourself. He states no other commandment is greater.

l: treasury, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus sits opposite the treasury and watches the multitude cast in money, with many rich people giving much. He observes that a poor widow's two small coins amounted to more than all the others gave.

l: poor widow, The Good News According to Mark
s: A poor widow drops two small brass coins, all she had to live on, into the treasury; Jesus tells his disciples she gave more than everyone else, giving from poverty.

l: temple, The Good News According to Mark
s: has_future_state completely thrown down [foretold by Jesus] The temple is the place Jesus leaves as a disciple remarks on its great stones and buildings. Jesus says that not one stone will be left on another that will not be thrown down.

l: abomination of desolation, The Good News According to Mark
s: spoken_of_by Daniel [prophet] Jesus says it was spoken of by Daniel the prophet and will be seen standing where it ought not, with the reader told to understand. When it is seen, those in Judea must flee to the mountains without taking anything from house or field.

l: great oppression (tribulation of those days), The Good News According to Mark
s: A tribulation Jesus describes as unparalleled in severity, never before or after. The Lord shortened its days for the chosen ones, otherwise no flesh would be saved. He urges prayer that flight not be in winter and warns of woe for pregnant and nursing women.

l: false christs and false prophets, The Good News According to Mark
s: performs signs and wonders [to lead astray even the chosen ones if possible] Jesus says they will arise and show signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones. He instructs the disciples not to believe anyone who says 'Look, here is the Christ!' or 'Look, there!'. Earlier, many who come in his name saying 'I am he!' are also said to lead many astray.

l: chosen ones, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_chosen_by God [picked out] The chosen ones are the reason the days of oppression are shortened, and false christs and prophets try to lead them astray if possible. At the coming of the Son of Man, his angels gather them from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of the sky.

l: coming of the Son of Man, The Good News According to Mark
s: The coming of the Son of Man follows the darkening of the sun and moon, falling stars, and shaken heavenly powers. People see him arrive in clouds with great power and glory; he sends angels to gather the chosen ones. Only the Father knows its day and hour.

l: watchfulness, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_commanded_to all [because the time is unknown] Jesus repeatedly commands watchfulness: be careful of being led astray, watch, keep alert, and pray, because no one knows when the time is. He closes by saying that what he tells the disciples he tells all: Watch!

l: woman (who anointed Jesus), The Good News According to Mark
s: remembered_for anointing Jesus [to be spoken of as a memorial wherever the Good News is preached] At Simon the leper's house in Bethany, the woman breaks an alabaster jar of costly pure nard ointment and pours it over Jesus' head. Some grumble that it was wasted, but Jesus says she did a good work and that what she did will be spoken of as a memorial to her wherever the Good News is preached.

l: Last Supper meal (bread and cup), The Good News According to Mark
s: represents body and blood of Jesus [blood of the new covenant] During the Passover meal Jesus blesses and breaks bread, giving it to the disciples and saying, "This is my body." He gives thanks over the cup, which they all drink, saying it is his blood of the new covenant poured out for many, and says he will not drink the fruit of the vine again until he drinks it anew in God's Kingdom.

l: Gethsemane, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_a place [where Jesus prayed] Gethsemane is the place where Jesus brings his disciples after the meal and takes Peter, James, and John further with him. There he prays, "Abba, Father," asking that the cup be removed yet submitting to the Father's will, finds the disciples sleeping three times, and is arrested.

l: crowd that arrested Jesus, The Good News According to Mark
s: An armed multitude with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, scribes, and elders, arrives with Judas and seizes Jesus after the kiss; Jesus protests being treated as a robber, saying Scriptures must be fulfilled.

l: young man in linen cloth, The Good News According to Mark
s: A young man in a white robe, sitting on the right side of Jesus' tomb, tells the astonished women not to be amazed, announces Jesus has risen, shows where he lay, and sends them to tell the disciples and Peter.

l: high priest, The Good News According to Mark
s: has_servant servant of the high priest The high priest receives Jesus after his arrest, asks why he does not answer the testimony against him, and asks if he is the Christ, the Son of the Blessed. When Jesus says "I am," he tears his clothes, declares it blasphemy, and the council condemns Jesus as worthy of death. One of his maids is the first to challenge Peter.

l: Peter's denial, The Good News According to Mark
s: foretold_by Jesus [before the rooster crows twice, three times] In the high priest's courtyard, Peter is identified as being with Jesus by a maid, again by the maid, and then by bystanders who note his Galilean speech. He denies it each time, the third time cursing and swearing he does not know the man, and the rooster crows a second time, fulfilling Jesus' prediction.

l: betrayal of Jesus, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus foretells that one of the twelve who eats with him will betray him, and says woe to that man. Judas carries it out by arranging with the chief priests, leading an armed crowd to Gethsemane, and identifying Jesus with a kiss, which leads to Jesus' arrest.

l: Pilate, The Good News According to Mark
s: Pilate is a governor who questions Jesus, marvels at his silence, and perceives the chief priests' envy. Wishing to please the multitude and following the feast custom of releasing a prisoner, he frees Barabbas and hands Jesus over after flogging to be crucified. Later, surprised at Jesus' death, he confirms it with the centurion and grants the body to Joseph.

l: multitude, The Good News According to Mark
s: The multitude asks Pilate to do as he always does and release a prisoner. Stirred up by the chief priests, they ask for Barabbas and cry out repeatedly "Crucify him!" even when Pilate asks what evil Jesus has done.

l: Barabbas, The Good News According to Mark
s: Barabbas, a prisoner bound with fellow insurgents who committed murder in the insurrection, is released by Pilate instead of Jesus at the crowd's request.

l: soldiers, The Good News According to Mark
s: The soldiers lead Jesus into the Praetorium and call together the whole cohort. They clothe him in purple, crown him with thorns, salute him as King of the Jews, strike him with a reed, spit on him and bow in mockery. They then lead him out to crucify him, compel Simon of Cyrene to carry the cross, and divide his garments by casting lots.

l: cross, The Good News According to Mark
s: The cross is carried to Golgotha by Simon of Cyrene, whom the soldiers compel to do so. Passersby and the chief priests taunt Jesus to come down from it.

l: crucifixion of Jesus, The Good News According to Mark
s: Jesus is crucified at Golgotha at the third hour beneath the inscription "THE KING OF THE JEWS," between two robbers, fulfilling Scripture. Mocked by all, he dies after darkness falls; the temple veil tears and the centurion declares him Son of God.

l: Mary Magdalene, The Good News According to Mark
s: Mary Magdalene, one of the women who watched from afar, was freed of seven demons by Jesus; she visits the tomb, flees in fear, then sees him first and tells disbelieving mourners.

l: Salome, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_one_of women [watched from afar] Salome buys spices with the two Marys and goes to the tomb to anoint Jesus. She is amazed by the young man's message, then flees afraid and says nothing.

l: Joseph of Arimathaea, The Good News According to Mark
s: Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member seeking God's Kingdom, boldly asks Pilate for Jesus' body, buys linen, wraps him, lays him in a rock-cut tomb, and rolls a stone against the door.

l: tomb (Jesus' tomb), The Good News According to Mark
s: A rock-cut tomb where Joseph of Arimathaea lays Jesus' linen-wrapped body, a stone rolled against its door while two Marys watch. Later the women find the very large stone rolled back, and a young man tells them Jesus has risen.

l: Mary the mother of James, The Good News According to Mark
s: is_mother_of James Mary the mother of James buys spices with the other women and goes to the tomb. She sees the young man, hears that Jesus has risen, and flees in trembling, telling no one.

l: disciples (of Jesus), The Good News According to Mark
s: includes Peter The disciples mourn and weep, and disbelieve Mary Magdalene's report and later that of the two who saw Jesus on a walk. Jesus appears to the eleven at the table and rebukes their unbelief and hardness of heart, then sends them to preach. They go out and preach everywhere, with the Lord working with them and confirming the word by signs.

l: resurrection of Jesus, The Good News According to Mark
s: The young man declares that Jesus, the crucified Nazarene, has risen and is not in the tomb. Jesus is then seen by Mary Magdalene, two others, and the eleven, though many who hear of it at first do not believe.

l: believers, The Good News According to Mark
s: Believers are those Jesus promises salvation if baptized; their belief is then marked by accompanying signs: casting out demons, new languages, handling serpents, surviving deadly drink, and healing the sick by laying on hands.

l: The Gospel According to Luke
s: This document is the Gospel of Luke, a 24-chapter narrative that opens with a preface to Theophilus and follows Jesus from before his birth to his ascension. Its central figure is Jesus; others who matter most include John the Baptizer, Mary, Peter and the twelve apostles, the Pharisees and scribes who oppose him, Judas, and Pilate. Chapters 1-2 tell of the angel Gabriel announcing the births of John to Zacharias and Elizabeth and of Jesus to Mary. Jesus is born in Bethlehem, welcomed by shepherds, Simeon and Anna, and at twelve is found among the teachers in the temple. Chapters 3-4 present John's baptism of repentance, Jesus' baptism with a voice from the sky calling him beloved Son, his genealogy back to Adam, and his temptation in the wilderness. He is then rejected at Nazareth and begins teaching and healing at Capernaum. Chapters 5-9 show his Galilean ministry: calling Simon, James, John and Levi, healing the leper and the paralytic, disputes over fasting and the Sabbath, choosing the twelve, and teaching blessings and woes. He heals a centurion's servant, raises a widow's son, and forgives a sinful woman. He teaches the parable of the sower, calms a storm, frees the Gadarene man, and raises Jairus' daughter. He sends out the twelve, feeds five thousand, and hears Peter's confession of him as the Christ. He foretells his suffering, is transfigured, and sets his face toward Jerusalem. Chapters 10-18 mostly occur on the journey. Jesus sends out seventy and tells the parable of the good Samaritan. He visits Martha and Mary, teaches prayer, and answers accusations of acting by Beelzebul. He pronounces woes on the Pharisees, warns against covetousness and anxiety, and calls people to repent. He laments over Jerusalem and teaches discipleship and humility. The parables of the lost sheep, coin and son, the shrewd manager, and Lazarus and the rich man follow, as do teachings on faith, the ten lepers, the Kingdom's coming, persistent prayer, the Pharisee and tax collector, and the rich ruler. Chapters 19-21 bring him to Jericho, where he meets Zacchaeus, and then into Jerusalem. He rides in as King, weeps over the city, cleanses the temple, and debates authority, taxes and resurrection with the leaders. He praises the widow's gift and foretells the temple's destruction and the coming of the Son of Man. Chapters 22-24 narrate the climax. Judas betrays Jesus, who shares the Passover meal, prays on the Mount of Olives, is arrested, and is denied by Peter. Pilate and Herod examine him, Pilate yields to the crowd, and Jesus is crucified, dies, and is buried by Joseph of Arimathaea. On the first day of the week the women find the tomb empty. Jesus appears to the Emmaus disciples and the eleven, opens the Scriptures to them, commissions them as witnesses, and is carried up into heaven.

l: Zacharias, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Zacharias is an aged, righteous priest of Abijah's division, married to Elizabeth. Gabriel tells him in the temple that she will bear John; he doubts and is struck mute. He regains speech by naming John, then prophesies, blessing God for redemption.

l: Elizabeth, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Elizabeth, righteous daughter of Aaron and wife of Zacharias, was barren and old yet conceived, hid five months, credited the Lord, blessed relative Mary, was filled with the Holy Spirit, and bore John.

l: John, The Gospel According to Luke
s: John is a prophet of the Most High, son of Zacharias, foretold by Gabriel as great before the Lord, abstaining from wine and strong drink, filled with the Holy Spirit from the womb, and going before God in the spirit and power of Elijah. He leaps in Elizabeth's womb, is born and named on the eighth day, and lives in the desert until appearing publicly to Israel. In the wilderness around the Jordan he preaches a baptism of repentance for remission of sins, baptizes with water, rebukes crowds, tax collectors, and soldiers, and announces one mightier who will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire. After reproving Herod, he is imprisoned. He has disciples, whom he teaches to pray, and sends two to ask Jesus whether he is the coming one. Jesus calls him a prophet and more, the greatest born of women, though some said he had a demon for his ascetic habits. All the people regarded him as a prophet.

l: Gabriel, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Gabriel is an angel who stands in God's presence; he announces John's birth to Zacharias, muting him for unbelief, then is sent to Mary in Nazareth to announce Jesus's conception.

l: Mary, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Mary is a virgin of Nazareth, betrothed to Joseph, who becomes the mother of Jesus. In Chapter 1, Gabriel tells her she has found favor with God; she accepts, visits Elizabeth, is called blessed, and sings praise. In Chapter 2 she travels to Bethlehem, gives birth to her firstborn, ponders the shepherds' sayings, hears Simeon say a sword will pierce her soul, and searches three days for the twelve-year-old Jesus. In Chapter 10, as Martha's sister, she sits at Jesus' feet and is said to have chosen the good part.

l: Joseph, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Joseph, son of Heli, lives in Nazareth and belongs to David's house. He travels to Bethlehem with Mary to enroll, witnesses the shepherds' visit and temple presentation, returns to Nazareth, and later he and Mary lose and find twelve-year-old Jesus in Jerusalem's temple at Passover.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Jesus is a individual presented as the foretold Son of the Most High and Son of God, a Savior, Christ and Lord, who is to receive David's throne and reign over the house of Jacob forever. The records follow his life from announcement to ascension. An angel names him before conception; he is born in Bethlehem as Mary's firstborn, presented at the temple, and at twelve tells the teachers he must be in his Father's house, then grows in wisdom and favor in Nazareth, subject to his parents. At about thirty he is baptized by John, a voice from the sky calls him beloved Son, and the Holy Spirit fills him. He resists the devil's temptations, and demons recognize him as Son of God and Christ. His mission is to preach the good news of God's Kingdom and to seek and save the lost. He teaches with authority in synagogues and the temple, heals lepers and the sick, casts out demons, commands wind and water, raises the dead, forgives sins as Son of Man, calls sinners to repentance, and claims to be lord of the Sabbath. He chooses twelve apostles, names Simon Peter, and later appoints and sends seventy, giving them authority; he says all things were delivered to him by the Father. He is homeless, habitually withdraws to pray, and is accused of gluttony and drunkenness. He sets his face toward Jerusalem, warns of Herod's threat, and foretells his suffering, death and rising. He enters Jerusalem acclaimed as King, teaches daily in the temple, and spends nights on Olivet. Betrayed by Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, he shares the Passover, is arrested, and before the council affirms he is the Son of God and will sit at God's right hand. Crucified between two criminals under the inscription King of the Jews, he commits his spirit to the Father, dies, and is buried in a tomb. He then rises with flesh and bones, is recognized at Emmaus in the breaking of bread, explains the Scriptures, tells the disciples to await the Father's promise, blesses them at Bethany, and is carried up into heaven.

l: Herod, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Herod, king of Judea with jurisdiction over Galilee, called a fox by Jesus. Long wanting to see a miracle, he gladly receives Jesus, questions him unanswered, mocks him with soldiers, robes him luxuriously, and returns him to Pilate, becoming Pilate's friend that day.

l: God, The Gospel According to Luke
s: God is presented across these records as the mighty, holy, merciful Father who is the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and of the living rather than the dead. Early on he swears an oath to Abraham, shows mercy to those who fear him across generations, and is called Lord of heaven and earth. In the opening chapters he sends Gabriel to Zacharias and Mary, hears Zacharias's request, and takes away Elizabeth's reproach. Mary and Zacharias praise him as Savior who has visited and redeemed his people and remembered his covenant. The heavenly army and shepherds glorify him, his law governs the circumcision and presentation of the child, and his grace rests on Jesus, who calls the temple his Father's house. The word of God comes to John, and a voice from the sky declares Jesus his beloved Son. A voice from the cloud later repeats this and tells hearers to listen to him. God sent Jesus, and whoever receives Jesus receives the one who sent him. Only the Father knows the Son, and the Son reveals the Father to whomever he desires. Jesus teaches that God is kind to the unthankful and evil and merciful as a Father, and that those who love enemies are children of the Most High. God is addressed in prayer as Father in heaven and gives the Holy Spirit to those who ask. He is also to be feared, since after killing he has power to cast into Gehenna. Yet he does not forget a single sparrow, feeds the ravens, clothes the lilies more splendidly than Solomon, and gives the Kingdom as his good pleasure. He knows the hearts of the Pharisees and regards what is exalted among men as an abomination. Later chapters stress his chosen ones, who cry to him day and night. He will avenge them quickly while exercising patience, and he alone is good. Things impossible with men are possible with God. The record closes with Jesus telling hearers to give to God what is God's, and describing God as God of the living, for all are alive to him.

l: Abraham, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Abraham, son of Terah, is addressed as father by a tormented rich man. He holds Lazarus at his bosom, explains reversed fortunes and an uncrossable gulf, and says the brothers have Moses and the prophets, unpersuaded even by resurrection.

l: David, The Gospel According to Luke
s: David is Jesse's son, who in Psalms calls the Christ 'Lord'; Jesus cites this in Chapter 20 to question how the Christ can be David's son.

l: Nazareth, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Nazareth is a city in Galilee built on a hill with a cliff brow. Joseph leaves it for Bethlehem, and the family returns there after Jerusalem. Jesus grows up there, obedient to his parents. Later he reads Isaiah in its synagogue; townspeople doubt him, grow wrathful, and lead him to the brow to throw him off, but he walks away.

l: temple, The Gospel According to Luke
s: The temple in Jerusalem, adorned with beautiful stones and gifts and containing a treasury, is where Jesus teaches daily. He first drives out buyers and sellers, calling it a house of prayer made a den of robbers, while leaders seek to destroy him but the people hang on his words. Later he foretells that not one stone will remain on another.

l: birth of John, The Gospel According to Luke
s: John's birth is foretold by Gabriel to Zacharias, and Elizabeth conceives afterward.
