When he is born, neighbors and relatives rejoice at the Lord's mercy, and on the eighth day Elizabeth and Zacharias both insist on the name John, which frees Zacharias's tongue and causes fear and talk throughout the hill country of Judea.

l: Gabriel's announcement of Jesus' conception, The Gospel According to Luke
s: In the sixth month of Elizabeth's pregnancy, Gabriel tells Mary in Nazareth that she will conceive and bear a son named Jesus. When she asks how, he says the Holy Spirit will come on her and the power of the Most High will overshadow her, notes Elizabeth's pregnancy as a sign, and says nothing spoken by God is impossible.

l: Bethlehem, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Bethlehem, David's city in Judea, is where Joseph enrolls as David's descendant, Jesus is born, and shepherds come to find the baby.

l: Jerusalem, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Jerusalem is a city central to Jesus's story. It first appears as the place of his presentation in the temple, where Simeon and Anna meet him, his parents bring him yearly for Passover, and at twelve he is found among the teachers. As Jesus travels toward it, he laments that it kills prophets and stones those sent to it, that it refused to be gathered by him, and that its house is left desolate. Approaching it from the Mount of Olives, he weeps, saying it did not know the time of its visitation, and predicts enemies surrounding it and leaving no stone on another. He foretells armies, desolation, death by the sword, captivity among nations, and trampling by Gentiles until their times are fulfilled. Finally, after his resurrection, Jerusalem is where the disciples gather, where Jesus appears, where repentance and forgiveness are to be preached to all nations beginning there, and where they wait to be clothed with power and return joyfully to the temple.

l: shepherds, The Gospel According to Luke
s: stays_in field [keeping watch by night over their flock] Shepherds keeping watch over their flock by night in the field are terrified when an angel of the Lord appears to them. They go with haste to Bethlehem, find Mary, Joseph, and the baby in the feeding trough, and publicize widely what had been said about the child. They return glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen.

l: angel (the angel of the Lord), The Gospel According to Luke
s: The angel of the Lord stands by the shepherds, the glory of the Lord shining around them, and tells them not to be afraid. He announces good news of great joy: a Savior, Christ the Lord, is born in David's city, and the sign is a baby wrapped in cloth lying in a feeding trough. A multitude of the heavenly army then joins him, and afterward the angels go away into the sky. It is also noted that the angel had given Jesus' name before he was conceived.

l: Simeon, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Simeon is a righteous, devout Jerusalem man with the Holy Spirit upon him, awaiting Israel's consolation. Told he would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ, he enters the temple, holds Jesus, blesses God for salvation, and tells Mary the child will cause Israel's falling and rising and a sword will pierce her soul.

l: Anna, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Anna is an aged prophetess, daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher. Married seven years, she was widowed about eighty-four years and never leaves the temple, worshiping with fasting and petitions. At the hour of Simeon's blessing, she thanks the Lord and speaks of Jesus to those awaiting redemption in Jerusalem.

l: enrollment (census), The Gospel According to Luke
s: A census decreed by Caesar Augustus for all the world, first held under Quirinius, governor of Syria; everyone enrolls in his own city, bringing Joseph and Mary from Nazareth to Bethlehem, where Jesus is born.

l: birth of Jesus, The Gospel According to Luke
s: has_place Bethlehem [laid in a feeding trough, no room in the inn] While Joseph and Mary are in Bethlehem for the enrollment, the day comes for Mary to give birth to her firstborn son. She wraps him in bands of cloth and lays him in a feeding trough because there was no room in the inn. An angel announces the birth to shepherds as the birth of a Savior, Christ the Lord, and the shepherds find the child as told.

l: presentation of Jesus at the temple, The Gospel According to Luke
s: takes_place_in Jerusalem [after purification days] When the days of purification according to the law of Moses are fulfilled, Joseph and Mary bring Jesus up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, as the law says every male who opens the womb shall be called holy, and to offer a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons. Simeon takes the child in his arms, blesses God, and speaks of him as salvation and a light for the nations, and Anna gives thanks and speaks of him. The parents then return to Nazareth after accomplishing everything the law required.

l: Passover, The Gospel According to Luke
s: also_called feast of unleavened bread The feast of unleavened bread, called the Passover, is approaching as the chief priests plot against Jesus. Jesus directs Peter and John to a large furnished upper room to prepare it. He says he has earnestly desired to eat this Passover with the apostles before he suffers and will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in God's Kingdom.

l: Pilate, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Pilate, governor of Judea, questions Jesus and three times finds no basis for a charge, sends him to Herod, becomes Herod's friend, then yields to the crowd, releases Barabbas, delivers Jesus, and grants Joseph the body.

l: Herod the tetrarch, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Herod is the tetrarch of Galilee who does evil, takes his brother's wife Herodias, is reproved by John, then imprisons John and, by his own statement, beheads him.

l: baptism of repentance, The Gospel According to Luke
s: John preaches it for remission of sins throughout the region around the Jordan. Those who undergo it are told to produce fruits worthy of repentance, and John contrasts it with the coming one's baptism in the Holy Spirit and fire; Jesus is also baptized among the people. Jesus asks whether John's baptism was from heaven or from men. The leaders reason that either answer would hurt them, since the people are persuaded John was a prophet, and they say they don't know.

l: multitudes (who came to John), The Gospel According to Luke
s: goes_out_to John [to be baptized] The multitudes go out to be baptized by John, who calls them offspring of vipers and warns them to produce good fruit and not rely on having Abraham as father. They ask what they must do and are told to share coats and food. The people are in expectation and wonder whether John is the Christ.

l: Christ, The Gospel According to Luke
s: The Christ is an awaited coming figure, whom people wondered John might be; popularly called David's son, a claim Jesus questions, noting David calls him Lord, leaving the puzzle unresolved.

l: Levi, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Levi, son of Melchi, is a tax collector who, called by Jesus to follow, leaves everything at his tax office, follows him, and hosts a great feast in his house.

l: Satan, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Satan, called the devil and linked to Beelzebul, prince of the demons, claims authority over the world's kingdoms. In Chapter 4 he tempts Jesus for forty days with bread, kingdoms for worship, and a temple leap, then departs after rebuffs. In Chapter 11, a crowd accuses Jesus of casting out demons by Beelzebul.

l: Capernaum, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Capernaum is a Galilean city with a synagogue, where Jesus, arriving from Nazareth, teaches on the Sabbath to astonished listeners, casts out a demon, and heals Simon's mother-in-law.

l: temptation of Jesus, The Gospel According to Luke
s: During forty days fasting in the wilderness, the devil tempts hungry Jesus three times: turning stone to bread, worshiping for kingdoms, jumping from the temple pinnacle. Jesus answers each with Scripture, and the devil departs until later.

l: synagogue (Nazareth), The Gospel According to Luke
s: is_located_in Nazareth In the Nazareth synagogue, Jesus stands on the Sabbath, as was his custom, and reads from the book of Isaiah. He declares the Scripture fulfilled in their hearing. His words there provoke wrath, and the people throw him out of the city.

l: synagogue crowd at Nazareth, The Gospel According to Luke
s: has_attitude_toward Jesus [wrath at his words] The crowd in the Nazareth synagogue fastens its eyes on Jesus and wonders at his gracious words, asking whether he is Joseph's son. After he cites a proverb and the examples of Elijah and Elisha, they are filled with wrath. They throw him out of the city and try to throw him off a cliff, but he passes through them.

l: unclean spirit man, The Gospel According to Luke
s: has_condition possessed by unclean demon [located in Capernaum synagogue] In the Capernaum synagogue a man with the spirit of an unclean demon cries out, calling Jesus of Nazareth the Holy One of God and asking whether he has come to destroy them. Jesus rebukes the spirit, which throws the man down in the middle of the people and comes out without harming him.

l: demons, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Demons are unclean spirits who recognize Jesus as the Christ and Son of God, and obey his authoritative commands. In Chapter 4 they cry out and are rebuked into silence. In Chapter 8 a multitude begs not to be sent to the abyss; Jesus lets them enter pigs, which drown in the lake.

l: Peter, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Peter, also called Simon, is a Galilean fisherman who owns boats and has partners James and John. After a miraculous catch at Jesus' word, he calls himself a sinful man, is told he will catch people, and leaves everything to follow Jesus. He becomes one of the twelve and one of the inner three, confesses Jesus as The Christ of God, and speaks unknowingly on the mountain. He vows to die with Jesus, yet after warning of Satan's sifting he denies Jesus three times, weeps bitterly, and is later expected to establish his brothers after turning again.

l: God's Kingdom, The Gospel According to Luke
s: God's Kingdom is the central subject of Jesus' teaching in these records: a reality that is both present and still to be entered. It begins in Chapter 9 as the message the twelve are sent to preach, demanding undivided commitment. In Chapter 10 the seventy announce that it has come near, and rejecting the messengers brings a harsher judgment than Sodom's. In Chapter 11 it is prayed for, and Jesus' casting out of demons shows it has come, in contrast to Satan's divided kingdom. In Chapter 12 disciples are told to seek it, and the Father gladly gives it to the little flock, so they need not fear. Chapter 13 describes it through the mustard seed and yeast, growing from small beginnings, and says people from every direction will sit down in it with Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and the prophets, while some are excluded and the last become first. In Chapter 17 Jesus tells the Pharisees it does not come with observation and is within them. Chapter 18 says it belongs to little children, that one must receive it like a child, that entry is very hard for the rich, and that those who leave family for its sake gain much now and eternal life.

l: multitude, The Gospel According to Luke
s: comes_from Judea, Jerusalem, Tyre and Sidon coast [came to hear him and be healed] A great number of people from all Judea, Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon gather on the level place to hear Jesus and be healed of diseases and unclean spirits. All the multitude seek to touch him because power comes out of him and heals them all.

l: catch of fish, The Gospel According to Luke
s: After Jesus tells Simon to put out into the deep, the nets take a great multitude of fish, so that the net begins to break. Partners in the other boat help, and both boats fill and begin to sink, amazing Simon, James, John, and the others.

l: man full of leprosy, The Gospel According to Luke
s: A man full of leprosy falls on his face before Jesus, asking to be made clean; Jesus touches him, wills it, and the leprosy leaves immediately. He is told to tell no one and show himself to the priest.

l: Pharisees, The Gospel According to Luke
s: The Pharisees are a group, often paired with scribes, teachers of the law and lawyers, who have disciples of their own and consistently oppose Jesus. Early on, having come from villages across Galilee, Judea and Jerusalem, they reason that he blasphemes in forgiving sins, murmur at his eating with tax collectors and sinners, question his disciples' fasting, and challenge plucking grain on the Sabbath. They watch him to accuse him, and after he heals a withered hand they are filled with rage. At a Sabbath meal, a Pharisee host marvels that he did not wash, and Jesus rebukes them: they cleanse the cup's outside while full of extortion and wickedness, tithe herbs while bypassing justice and love, love the best seats, and are like hidden graves. They grow angry and lie in wait to catch his words. Later they stay silent when asked about healing on the Sabbath, murmur again about his welcoming sinners, warn him about Herod, and, described as lovers of money, scoff, justifying themselves before men while God knows their hearts.

l: paralyzed man, The Gospel According to Luke
s: A paralyzed man, carried on a cot by men and lowered through tiles before Jesus, is forgiven his sins, told to rise, and immediately walks home glorifying God.

l: forgiveness of sins, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Forgiveness of sins is regarded by the Pharisees as belonging to God alone. In Chapter 5, Jesus forgives a paralyzed man and heals him to show the Son of Man's authority on earth to forgive. In Chapter 7, he links forgiveness to love through the two debtors parable, forgives the woman, and the table guests wonder who he is.

l: sinners, The Gospel According to Luke
s: comes_close_to Jesus [to hear him] The tax collectors and sinners were all coming close to Jesus to hear him. They are the ones the Pharisees and scribes complain he welcomes and eats with.

l: feast at Levi's house, The Gospel According to Luke
s: has_attendees tax collectors [great crowd] Levi hosts a great feast for Jesus at his house, attended by a great crowd of tax collectors and others. The scribes and Pharisees murmur against the disciples for eating and drinking with sinners, and Jesus answers that the sick need a physician and that he came to call sinners to repentance.

l: disciples (Jesus's disciples), The Gospel According to Luke
s: The disciples are Jesus's followers, a group from whom he chooses twelve as apostles. They do not fast while the bridegroom is with them, and they are given knowledge of the mysteries of God's Kingdom, unlike others who get parables. In Chapter 6 they pluck grain on the Sabbath and are questioned, then receive Jesus's teaching on love, mercy and not judging. In Chapter 8 they ask about the sower parable, fear the storm and marvel at his power; Peter, John and James enter Jairus' house. In Chapter 17 they learn about stumbling blocks and forgiveness, ask for more faith, and are warned about false claims of 'Look, here!'

l: fasting, The Gospel According to Luke
s: will_be_practiced_by Jesus' disciples [after the bridegroom is taken away] Jesus is asked why John's disciples and the Pharisees' disciples often fast and pray while his disciples eat and drink. He answers that the friends of the bridegroom cannot be made to fast while the bridegroom is with them, but that when he is taken away, they will fast in those days.

l: parable of garments and wineskins, The Gospel According to Luke
s: teaches new must not be mixed with old [new wine needs fresh wineskins] Jesus tells that no one puts a piece of a new garment on an old one, and no one puts new wine into old wineskins, since the new would tear the old garment and burst the skins. New wine must go into fresh wineskins, and he adds that no one who has drunk old wine immediately desires new, saying 'The old is better.'

l: Sabbath, The Gospel According to Luke
s: The Sabbath is a day on which Jesus healed, and healing on it provoked indignation. Across three chapters it becomes the setting of repeated conflict. In Chapter 6, plucking grain and healing a withered hand lead Jesus to call the Son of Man lord of the Sabbath and ask whether it is lawful to do good or save life. In Chapter 13, a synagogue ruler objects to a bent woman's healing, and Jesus cites watering an ox. In Chapter 14, at a Sabbath meal, observers watch him and he cites rescuing a son or ox from a well.

l: man with the withered hand, The Gospel According to Luke
s: has_condition withered right hand A man with a withered right hand is in the synagogue on a Sabbath. Jesus, knowing the thoughts of those watching, has him stand in the middle and tells him to stretch out his hand, and it is restored as sound as the other.

l: the twelve, The Gospel According to Luke
s: The twelve are the apostles Jesus chooses from his disciples after a night of prayer, named in a list that ends with Judas Iscariot, the future traitor. Given power over demons and disease, they are sent to preach and heal, yet they misunderstand, fail to cast out a spirit, and argue about greatness. At the Passover meal Jesus promises them a kingdom and thrones judging Israel's twelve tribes. On the Mount of Olives they sleep from grief, and Judas leads the arresting crowd.

l: Judas Iscariot, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve apostles, is a traitor. Satan enters him, and he bargains with chief priests and captains to deliver Jesus for money. Jesus notes his betrayer is at the table; Judas then leads the crowd and approaches to kiss Jesus.

l: Beatitudes and woes, The Gospel According to Luke
s: addresses disciples [spoken to his disciples] Jesus blesses the poor, the hungry, the weeping, and those hated for the Son of Man's sake, promising God's Kingdom, fullness, laughter, and great reward in heaven. He pronounces woes on the rich, the full, those who laugh now, and those of whom men speak well, warning of hunger, mourning, and the pattern of the fathers with the false prophets.

l: enemies, The Gospel According to Luke
s: are_to_be loved [Jesus's command] Jesus commands his hearers to love their enemies, do good to those who hate them, bless those who curse them, and pray for those who mistreat them. He says doing so, and lending expecting nothing back, brings great reward and makes them children of the Most High.

l: love and mercy, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Jesus teaches the golden-rule standard of doing to others as one would like done to oneself and says loving only those who love you earns no credit, since sinners do the same. He urges being merciful as the Father is merciful, not judging or condemning, setting free, and giving generously, with the same measure returned.

l: wise and foolish builders, The Gospel According to Luke
s: A parable in Chapter 6 where Jesus asks why people call him 'Lord' yet disobey. Hearing and doing his words is like building on rock, so the house withstands the flood; hearing without doing is like building without foundation, so the house collapses in ruin.

l: centurion, The Gospel According to Luke
s: A centurion who commands soldiers and loves his dear servant. Admired for loving the Jewish nation and building their synagogue, he sends elders and friends to ask Jesus to heal the servant, declaring himself unworthy. Recognizing authority, he trusts Jesus's word, and Jesus praises his faith as unmatched in Israel.

l: servant (the centurion's servant), The Gospel According to Luke
s: The centurion's servant was sick and at the point of death. When the men sent by the centurion returned to the house, they found that the servant was well.

l: widow of Nain, The Gospel According to Luke
s: A widow of Nain, mourning her only son at his funeral procession, is shown compassion by Jesus, who tells her not to cry, raises her son, and returns him to her.

l: young man (the widow's son), The Gospel According to Luke
s: has_state restored to life [raised by Jesus] The widow's only son was dead and being carried out of Nain in a coffin. Jesus touched the coffin and told him to arise, and he sat up and began to speak, after which Jesus gave him to his mother.

l: disciples of John, The Gospel According to Luke
s: John's disciples told him about Jesus' works, and two of them were sent to Jesus with John's question about whether he was the coming one. Jesus told them to report to John what they had seen and heard: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news preached to them.

l: lawyers, The Gospel According to Luke
s: Lawyers are a group rebuked by Jesus in Chapter 11 after one objects to being insulted; he pronounces woes on them for burdening people without helping, building prophets' tombs their fathers killed, and removing the key of knowledge.
